title: Oncall rotation synthesis — 2027-11-15
content:
Purpose:
This note captures synthesis from the oncall rotation covering 2027-11-08 to 2027-11-15. It combines incident summaries, SLO health, runbook tweaks, and handoff reminders for the incoming rotation. Mostly rough notes — use for the weekly async sync and to seed the postmortem where appropriate.

High-level summary:
- Week was mostly stable: 99.85% latency SLO met for the week, but two incidents consumed ~40% of the remaining error budget for the month.
- Main recurring theme: intermittent KV cache invalidation across Dedicated inference pools when autoscaler restarted nodes – surfaced heavy tail latency spikes.
- Action focus: make autoscaler restarts graceful, add cache-warm path to serving runtime, improve alert thresholds to reduce noisy pagers.

Incidents (short):
1) INC-2027-11-12: "Serving runtime cache-miss storm" — 2027-11-12 02:42 UTC
   - Impact: ~6 minutes of 95th/99th latency spikes for hosted-api routes; small fraction of requests returned 502 for clients using large-seq models.
   - Probable cause: orchestration race during node replacement -> KV cache invalidation + cold kv-writes under burst traffic.
   - Mitigation: temporarily scaled dedicated pool + enabled fallback model variant (lower mem) for high-latency customers.
   - Current status: triaged, follow-up RFC opened (SRE-4821).
   - Owner/action: Samir to prototype cache-warm on node join; ETA 2027-11-30.

2) INC-2027-11-10: "DNS flapping to region eu-west-1" — 2027-11-10 11:10 UTC
   - Impact: routing glitches for a segment of Dedicated customers in EU; retries recovered most flows within 90s.
   - Root cause: transient edge LB mismatch after an automated cert rotation.
   - Mitigation: manual rollback of cert job; added extra verification to cert pipeline.
   - Owner/action: Ethan to add pre-flight LB-checks in the cert rotation job (PR in review).

SLO / Error budget snapshot:
- Latency SLO (p95 < 120ms): week target met at 99.85% (monthly rolling currently 99.2%, error budget remaining 0.8%).
- Availability SLO (99.95% monthly): monthly running at 99.88% (tight).
- Observations: two incidents used ~0.12 of monthly budget. If we hit one more similar incident, we’ll breach. Recommend conservative rollout settings on capacity changes.

Runbook and process notes:
- Runbook change #1: Add a "node join cache warm" checklist under Serving Runtime > KV Cache section. (See PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/98)
- Runbook change #2: Update Pager thresholds to include a "kv-cache-pressure" indicator to reduce alert noise from benign transient misses. Maya to draft language.
- Playbook gap: no clear fallback for long-tail tokenization failures in dedup layer; added as a TODO for research.

Handoff / operational reminders for next rotation:
- Incoming oncall (Nov 15–22): Jules is primary, Maya backup. Handoff checklist:
  - Confirm autoscaler gracefulRestart flag enabled in env-staging before promoting to prod.
  - Validate that SRE dashboard shows KV cache hit-rate > 98% for the prior 6 hours.
  - Check INC-2027-11-12 follow-ups; verify Samir's cache-warm PR progress.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Samir Rao: Prototype and bench cache-warm on node join; initial perf numbers and failure modes documented. ETA 2027-11-30.
- Ethan Clarke: Add LB pre-flight check to cert rotation job + e2e test. ETA 2027-11-22.
- Maya Patel: Draft kv-cache-pressure alert wording + update runbook. ETA 2027-11-19.
- Priya Menon: Run an oncall war-room simulation focused on autoscaler restart paths. ETA 2027-12-03.

Notes to self / loose threads:
- Investigate correlation between high token-length requests and cache thrash — Jupyter sketch exists in repo/sre/experiments/token-length-impact.ipynb.
- Evaluate whether automatic fallback to a quantized model variant reduces tail latency without harming quality; run small AB test on internal traffic.
- Consider temporarily increasing error budget guardrails for Dedicated during holiday peak cadence.

Meeting follow-ups for ASYNC sync (this doc -> weekly SRE async):
- Attach incident timeline and packet captures to INC ticket.
- Decide whether INC-2027-11-12 warrants a full postmortem (propose: blameless writeup if impact >5 minutes AND >1% traffic affected).

Quick links used in notes:
- INC ticket: INC-2027-11-12
- RFC for cache changes: SRE-4821
- Runbooks PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/98
- Slack: #sre-ops, #platform-alerts

If anything's missing or someone wants to add rough notes before the async thread, drop them here — this will be the canonical oncall rotation synthesis for the week.

-- Priya
